title: Pay transfer (stamp) duty when buying land or other dutiable property
what: The buyer (transferee) of land or other dutiable property pays transfer duty on the transfer, at the rates the Act sets.

sources.title: Duties Act 2001 (Tas)
sources.quote: 11. Who is liable to pay the duty? Duty charged by this Chapter is payable by the transferee, unless this Chapter requires another person to pay the duty.

administration.who: State Revenue Office Tasmania (Commissioner of State Revenue)

sources.title: Duties Act 2001 (Tas)
sources.locator: s 3, words naming the body (found 18 Nov 2026) (current)
sources.quote: Commissioner means the Commissioner of State Revenue appointed as such under the Taxation Administration Act 1997 ;

reach.condition: if it buys land or other dutiable property in the state

sources.title: Duties Act 2001 (Tas)
sources.quote: 11. Who is liable to pay the duty? Duty charged by this Chapter is payable by the transferee, unless this Chapter requires another person to pay the duty.

confidence_note: The Act's own words make the buyer (or the parties) liable for the duty.

assessment.summary: A tax on buying a home, paid every time property changes hands. It discourages people from moving, including for work, and is one of the least efficient taxes in Australia; a broad annual land tax raising the same revenue would cost far less.

marks.reason: A transaction tax in the largest asset market, with an efficiency cost Treasury puts at 72 cents per extra dollar raised.
Raises the cost of moving home, so fewer people move to take better jobs.
